purpose: Test whether the trained programming tail helps as a checked extra attempt versus giving the unchanged parent the same extra decode and output-token cap. The repair prompt is longer, so wall-clock compute is not claimed equal.
policy: Generate the unchanged parent once. If the public example from the prompt passes, keep that program. Otherwise generate one extra answer: the trained expert on the original prompt, versus the parent on the frozen repair conversation. Score every arm on the full withheld test list, including extra attempts that repeat the first-answer tokens. Record input tokens, output tokens and public-example checking time. Do not train. Do not open the original 128-task final.
selection: Reuse the rejected trial's trained tail without further updates. Pin that checkpoint, tokenizer, selected parent plan and leftover task IDs before any new generation. The opened-development 15/32 diagnostic cannot pass this experiment.
scope: Operated inference-only comparison. MBPP leftovers from the original final pool, never previously generated by this trial. No NEURO issuance, no promotion, no original-final opening, no cheaper-verification claim.
